fields.meta_title: Occupational Therapy Intake Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an occupational therapy intake form that asks which daily tasks are hard and saves every answer to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Occupational Therapy Intake Form Around Daily Tasks
fields.hero_description: Build an occupational therapy intake form that records the daily tasks each patient wants back, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Therapist Knows Before the Evaluation
fields.features_subheading: Describe your caseload, and Emergent builds an occupational therapy intake form around the daily tasks patients want to get back.
fields.feature_1:
Daily tasks the patient marks as hard

Give patients a checklist of daily tasks such as getting dressed, cooking, writing, and opening jars. They tick the hard ones, and the therapist starts the evaluation there.
fields.feature_2:
Injured hand and writing hand, asked apart

Ask about the injured hand and the hand the patient writes with as separate questions. When both answers name the same hand, a Dominant hand label sits at the top of the chart.
fields.feature_3:
Pediatric sections that follow the child's age

A parent enters the child's age first. School questions about the grade and the teacher's main concern appear only for children 5 and older, and younger ones skip them.
fields.feature_4:
Goals the patient rates from 1 to 10

Patients name the activities they most want back and rate how well they manage each one from 1 to 10. The same goals return at re-evaluation, and both ratings sit side by side.
fields.feature_5:
A front desk list for missing referrals

Ask for the referring physician on every intake. An intake that arrives with that field blank goes to a front desk list, so staff can call the patient before anything is booked.
fields.feature_6:
The codebase in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the code for the intake form and its chart screens to your GitHub repository. A developer can host it on the clinic's own servers and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Where the Answers Go in Four OT Practices
fields.tab_content_1:
Every child 5 or older gets school questions

Fernwold Pediatric Therapy asks each parent for the child's age first. Bettina Ellingboe enters 7 for her son Soren, and the school section opens. She ticks buttons and zippers as hard at home, picks 2nd grade, and types handwriting as the teacher's main concern. Wilhelmina Mwale reads it all before his evaluation.
fields.tab_content_2:
A label when the injured hand is the writing hand

Hollybank Hand Therapy asks every new patient two questions: which hand was injured, and which hand they write with. When the injured hand is the writing hand, the chart gets a Dominant hand label. Lorcan Osei-Bonsu answers left to both, and Henrike Ravindran sees the label before his 2:15 evaluation.
fields.tab_content_3:
No referral on the intake, no slot on the calendar

Pinmoor Driver Rehab books a driving evaluation only when the intake names a referring physician. The form also asks for license status and when the patient last drove. Thaddeus Ellwood fills in both but leaves the physician blank. His intake goes to Saoirse Kowal's front desk list, and she calls him for the name.
fields.tab_content_4:
By week 8, all four goals are rated again

Hartsmere Occupational Therapy asks new patients for the activities that matter most, each rated from 1 to 10. Philippa Northcote picks cooking dinner, gardening, typing emails, and carrying groceries, at 3, 2, 4, and 5. At week 8 she rates the same four again: 7, 6, 8, and 7. Ngozi Petrakis sees both columns side by side.

fields.howto_title: Create an Occupational Therapy Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an occupational therapy intake form that shows the therapist what is hard for each patient before the evaluation.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide who answers for the patient
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give each caseload its own section
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Let patients write their own goals
fields.howto_step_1_des: Read back through recent evaluations and write down the tasks patients came in unable to do, such as bathing, buttoning a shirt, chopping vegetables, or getting in and out of a car. That list becomes the checklist on the first screen.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Adults answer for themselves, and a parent answers for a young child. Add a Completed by question at the top. The therapist then knows whose view each answer gives.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A clinic that sees both children and drivers needs different questions for each. Put them in separate sections and show a section only when the earlier answers call for it. Nobody scrolls past questions meant for someone else.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Leave the goal questions open. "Lift my granddaughter" tells the therapist more than a box marked shoulder strength, and the patient recognizes the goal when it comes back at re-evaluation.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the sections and the rules for when each one opens into one prompt. Emergent builds the intake form and the database behind it. Ask in plain English when a question needs rewording later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Ask for a chart screen per patient
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have the chart open on the tasks the patient marked as hard, with the goals under them. The therapist can read it in the few minutes before the evaluation instead of paging through a packet.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form once as the parent of a 4-year-old and check that the school section stays closed. Then fill it in as an adult with the referring physician left blank, and look for that intake on the front desk list.

faq_plan.q: What is an occupational therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: An occupational therapy intake form is the questionnaire a patient, or a parent for a child, fills in before the first OT evaluation. Occupational therapists evaluate and treat people who have injuries, illnesses, or disabilities, and the intake tells them which everyday tasks have become hard. It also records the referral and the goals the patient wants to work toward.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an occupational therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: List the sections your clinic needs and when each should appear, then put it all in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds a working form, and every answer is saved to a database you own. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What daily living questions belong on an occupational therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: Ask about self-care first, then the tasks that run a household and a job. Self-care covers dressing, bathing, eating, and using the toilet, and the second group covers cooking, shopping, driving, and work. Those tasks are the work itself: occupational therapists help clients relearn and perform daily living tasks, such as teaching a person who has had a stroke how to get dressed.

faq_plan.q: How is an occupational therapy intake form different from a counseling intake?
faq_plan.a: It starts with what the patient can do, not how they feel. A therapy intake form for counseling can open with mood screeners and a match to a clinician. An OT intake opens with the daily tasks that have become hard and where each one happens, whether at home, at school, or on the job.

faq_plan.q: Who should fill out a pediatric occupational therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: The parent or guardian fills it in for a young child. Let an older child add a few answers in their own words. Some occupational therapists work with children in inpatient, outpatient, or educational settings, and the intake should ask which of those sent the child. Add a short section for the teacher's observations when school is where the trouble shows.

faq_plan.q: How do I use an occupational therapy intake form to track goal progress?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the same goal ratings at each re-evaluation and keep both sets on one screen. In the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure, the client rates five chosen priority areas using 10-point scales on two domains, then scores each of the five again later. Emergent builds a chart screen that lines up both sets when you describe it.

faq_plan.q: Can one occupational therapy intake form also cover acupuncture patients?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the shared part stays short. Put contact details and the referral in one opening section, then branch on the service booked. A patient booked for OT gets the daily tasks and goals, and a patient booked for needling gets the acupuncture intake form questions instead.

faq_plan.q: Can patients answer an occupational therapy intake form one question at a time?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask Emergent for a conversational flow that shows one question per screen instead of one long page. It helps a patient typing with an injured hand, who sees one short answer at a time. Keep the daily tasks as a checklist on a single screen, so a patient taps every hard task in one place.

faq_plan.q: Where should occupational therapy intake form responses be stored?
faq_plan.a: Store them where your clinic controls who can see them and where they sit next to the patient's chart. The app Emergent builds saves every intake to a database you own. When your practice software has an API, the app can sync each intake into it.

faq_plan.q: Should an OT practice build its own occupational therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but start from a general patient intake form and add the OT sections to it. Contact details and the referral carry over unchanged. The daily tasks checklist and the goal ratings are what make it an OT intake, and keeping them in the same form puts every answer on one chart.

plan.angle: The SERP for this query has no top 10 in the workbook, and the AlsoAsked tree drifts into OT careers and autism therapy. Generic intake templates ask for a diagnosis and stop. This page wins by building the intake around what occupational therapy treats: the daily tasks a patient cannot do now, which hand is injured and which one writes, age-based pediatric sections, a referral check for driving evaluations, and goals the patient rates from 1 to 10 and rates again at re-evaluation.
